corePrinciples: Making the pitch as large as possible when in possession to facilitate passing
Compressing the pitch as small as possible out of possession to strangle opposition playmakers
Maintaining compact vertical distances ('short team' principle) to deny possession to opponents
Structured exploitation of spaces via pre-programmed coalition actions

4-3-3.summary: Forged in Dutch Total Football and refined under Pep Guardiola's juego de posición, characterized by absolute positional discipline, a single defensive screen acting as a deep playmaker, and a front line of inverted wingers and a false nine.

buildOut.shape: 4-3-3 base shape with goalkeeper (1), back four (5, 4, 3, 2), single pivot DM (6), central midfielders (10, 8), and front three (11, 9, 7).
roles: GK (Menzo) initiates possession from defensive third
CBs (Hulshoff, Koeman) provide deep build-out platform
DM (Busquets) acts as deep playmaker screen
patterns: Circulation through defensive third to single pivot
Vertical passing lanes opened by coordinated spacing
oppositionNotes: Maintains vertical compactness to resist high pressing

progression.shape: Midfield circulation shape maintaining positional discipline and passing lanes.
roles: CMs (Mühren, Neeskens) circulate ball through midfield
Full-backs (Krol, Suurbier) advance along flanks
patterns: Flank Triangle formation activation on the wings
Midfield passing combinations between pivots and interior runners
oppositionNotes: Exploits space created by manipulating central defenders

attack.shape: Inverted attacking structure with false nine and inverted wingers.
roles: CF (Cruyff / Messi / False 9) drops into central pockets to manipulate defenders
Inverted wingers (Villa, Stoichkov, Swart, Keizer) cut inside
Overlapping or advancing full-backs provide wide width
patterns: False nine dropping deep to overload midfield lanes
Winger diagonal cuts inside to open space for overlapping full-backs
Flank triangle combinations
oppositionNotes: Drags central defenders out of position to create penetrative gaps

4-4-2.summary: Pioneered by Viktor Maslov and immortalized by Arrigo Sacchi's AC Milan, relying on strict zonal marking, an integrated sliding back-four, and a compact 'short team' block of no more than 25 meters.

buildOut.shape: 4-4-2 compact defensive and midfield block with goalkeeper (1), back four (5, 2, 6, 3), flat midfield four (11, 8, 4, 7), and front two strikers (10, 9).
roles: GK (Galli) initiates from back
Back four (Maldini, Baresi, Costacurta, Tassotti) maintains strict zonal alignment
patterns: Integrated sliding back-four movement
Short team block build-out keeping within 25 meters
oppositionNotes: Maintains defensive stability and immediate cover across zones

roles: Central midfielders (Rijkaard, Ancelotti) distribute play
LM (Evani) and RM (Donadoni) manage flank transitions
patterns: Asymmetrical wing progression where one wide midfielder tucks inside
Platform creation for opposite winger and overlapping full-back
oppositionNotes: Denies central progression passing lanes to opposition playmakers

attack.shape: Attacking configuration featuring target hold-up play and asymmetrical width.
roles: LST (van Basten - Runner) makes penetrative runs
RST (Gullit - Hold Up) provides target man hold-up play
RM (Donadoni - Tucked) tucks inside, LB/RB (Anderson/Maldini - Overlap/Tucked) coordinate overlapping width
patterns: Target man hold-up combined with dynamic runner off the shoulder
One wide midfielder tucks inside while opposite full-back overlaps wide
oppositionNotes: Overwhelms defensive lines through synchronized strike partnership and flank acceleration

4-2-3-1.summary: Introduced by Juanma Lillo as a symmetrical way to deploy four forwards while maintaining defensive cover using a 'doble pivot' and a central number 10 orchestrator.

buildOut.shape: 4-2-3-1 base with goalkeeper (1), center-backs (4, 3), double pivot holding midfielders (8, 6), and full-backs (5, 2).
roles: GK (1) distributes to center-backs
Double pivot holding midfielders (LDM/RDM) shield center-backs and provide immediate passing lanes
patterns: Symmetrical build-out through center-backs and double pivot
Quick horizontal and vertical circulation in defensive third
oppositionNotes: Provides secure defensive cover during initial build-out

progression.shape: Midfield transition shape connecting double pivot to the trequartista zone.
roles: Double pivot circulating to central attacking midfielder (CAM)
Wingers (RAM, LAM) positioning in half-spaces
patterns: Progressing ball centrally into the #10 pocket
Symmetrical ball advancement through wide and central channels
oppositionNotes: Overloads central midfield zones to bypass opposition pressing blocks

attack.shape: Advanced attacking shape featuring four forwards and overlapping fullbacks.
roles: ST (Focal Point) pins central defenders
CAM (Playmaker) orchestrates in the trequartista zone
RAM / LAM (Inverted) cut inside
RB / LB (Overlap) push up wide
patterns: Inverted wingers cutting inside to clear space for overlapping fullbacks
Central orchestrator feeding penetrative balls to the focal point striker
oppositionNotes: Maintains high defensive pressure and numerical superiority in the final third

3-5-2.summary: Devised by Carlos Bilardo, Ciro Blažević, and Sepp Piontek to integrate a free-spirited playmaker without defensive compromise by deploying a central back-three and high wing-backs for a five-man midfield overload.

buildOut.shape: 3-5-2 defensive structure with goalkeeper (1), central back-three consisting of sweeper/libero flanked by two markers (5, 4, 3), and defensive midfielder (8).
roles: GK (Qvist) initiates play
CB / Libero (M. Olsen) acts as sweeper-playmaker
RCB (Busk) and LCB (Nielsen) provide marking cover
patterns: Libero stepping out from defense into midfield to create numerical superiority
Triangular passing network between back-three and deep midfielder
oppositionNotes: Three central defenders counter lone-striker systems effectively

roles: DM (Bertelsen / Batista Screen) anchors central progression
LCM (Lerby) and RCM (Berggreen) circulate possession
RWB (Sivebæk) and LWB (J. Olsen) push high
patterns: Establishing a 5-man midfield overload
Transitioning ball rapidly from back-three to advanced wing-backs
oppositionNotes: Overwhelms opponent midfield lines through sheer numbers

attack.shape: Attacking shape with advanced wing-backs, free-role playmaker, and dual strikers.
roles: AM (Maradona - Free Role / 10) operates between lines
ST / RST / LST (Valdano, Elkjaer, Laudrup) provide dual central attacking focal points
RWB / LWB (Advanced) act as flank runners providing width
patterns: Wing-backs pushing high to attack the flanks in the absence of traditional wingers
Playmaker exploiting space in advanced pockets behind twin strikers
Overloading wide and central attacking channels simultaneously
oppositionNotes: Repurposes traditional fullbacks into high attacking threats while maintaining secure central defensive coverage

boardImplications: Build-out phase: Position goalkeeper and center-backs deep to establish numerical superiority, anchoring with either a single pivot (#6), a double pivot (doble pivot), or a back-three with a libero.

Progression phase: Form compact vertical lines (maintaining 'short team' distances under 25 meters) while utilizing triangles and half-space positioning (inverted wingers, tucking wide midfielders, or 5-man midfield overloads) to circulate the ball safely.

Attacking phase: Create width via overlapping full-backs or advanced wing-backs while manipulating central defenders using false nines, dropping #10s, or inverted wingers cutting inside into pocket spaces.
Defensive transition: Ensure instant zonal recovery and sliding back-four/back-three alignment to seal vertical passing lanes and deny space to opposition playmakers.
